findings.description: The fix-up's new parenthetical misattributes reaching fifteen user-invoked skills to decision 19 alone: decision 19's six skills include `caveman` and `pr-description`, neither of which is user-invoked (no `disable-model-invocation` key), so it only takes the count from 9 to 13; decision 21 (restoring `pr-ci-review` and `review-retro`) is what closes the gap to 15.
findings.body:
The fix-up commit's new parenthetical says the jump from nine to fifteen user-invoked skills happens "(fifteen once decision 19 landed the rest of the template's skills; the frontmatter is the authoritative list)". Checked against the frontmatter this line calls authoritative: Decision 19 lands six skills (`grill-me`, `grill-with-docs`, `improve-codebase-architecture`, `caveman`, `find-dead-code`, `pr-description`), but `caveman` and `pr-description` carry no `disable-model-invocation` key in their real frontmatter — they're model-invoked. So decision 19 only adds 4, taking the count from 9 to 13, not 15. The remaining 2 (`pr-ci-review`, `review-retro`) are what decision 21 restores ("Decision 16 dropped `pr-ci-review` and `review-retro` ... so the pipeline ships too"), not decision 19.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agent-init/blob/623426b4fec98c3cb1ba0b7a906abda79caea8a9/docs/design/0001-architecture.md#L351-L354
findings.suggestion:
**Cost accepted: user-only skills are not user-only everywhere.** Nine skills at this point are
meant to fire only when a human names them, marked with `disable-model-invocation: true` (fifteen
once decision 19 added four more and decision 21 restored `pr-ci-review` and `review-retro`; the
frontmatter is the authoritative list). Verified 2026-09-17, only

findings.description: The new sentence closing the Codex-second-step gap cites `docs/capability-matrix.md`, but this file is scaffolded into consumer repos via the `thinking` pack while `docs/capability-matrix.md` is agent-init's own internal doc that never ships there — a dangling reference and a direct instance of what Decision 7 forbids ("Ported skills must not reference repo-specific convention paths").
findings.body:
The new sentence closing the Codex-second-step gap cites `docs/capability-matrix.md` as where opencode/Vibe's behavior is recorded. But this file (`SKILL-MECHANICS.md`) ships into consumer repositories as part of the `thinking` pack (`src/plan.utils.ts:20`, copied via the pack's copy-dir action) — `docs/capability-matrix.md` is agent-init's own internal doc and is never scaffolded there. This is a direct instance of what Decision 7 forbids: "Ported skills must not reference repo-specific convention paths." A consumer who follows the citation in their own repo finds nothing there.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/agent-init/blob/623426b4fec98c3cb1ba0b7a906abda79caea8a9/templates/agents/skills/writing-for-agents/SKILL-MECHANICS.md#L10
findings.suggestion: - A **user-invoked** skill strips the description from the agent's reach: only the human typing its name can invoke it, and no other skill can. Zero context load, but it spends cognitive load: you are the index that must remember it exists. Mechanics: set `disable-model-invocation: true`; the `description` becomes human-facing: a one-line summary, trigger lists stripped. That key is enough on Claude Code and Cursor. Codex ignores it and reads `agents/openai.yaml` beside the `SKILL.md` instead, so a user-invoked skill needs that file too, carrying `policy:` / `  allow_implicit_invocation: false`; opencode and Mistral Vibe honour neither, and the model can fire the skill there. Copy the file from any user-invoked skill: a test asserts every one of them has it, byte for byte, because Codex silently ignores a copy it cannot parse.

findings.description: The new sentence says "a test asserts every one of them has it, byte for byte", but `test/skill-invocation.test.ts` strips comments and blank lines and only compares the two-line `policy:` payload (comments are explicitly free to vary); Decision 22 elsewhere in the repo already describes this correctly as "line for line", which this sentence should match.

process_issues.description: Both reviewer subagents and the orchestrator hit the sandbox's approval gate on plain multi-line Bash constructs (for loops, chained && / ; commands) even though read-only; worked around with single unchained git show/grep commands per file. Same friction as the prior review round on this PR.
